method.sampling: 20 m lattice offsets inside radius b/2, DEM bilinear-interpolated at 50 m product pixel centres

step5_profile_vs_grid.definition: ratio = median two-point |slope| from LDEM grid columns (y direction) / area-weighted median of the PGDA-70 along-track map over pixels with centres inside the window

plane_fit_vs_profile.note: median plane-fit slope at b = 200 m (2-D gradient magnitude) over the PGDA-70 225 m along-track median

caveats: NASA roughness uses residuals of individual LOLA spots about the plane; ours uses DEM samples only (no access to spots here), so our roughness is expected to be lower, mostly where spots carry sub-pixel relief.

The paper does not state the exact positions of the 81 points nor the interpolation; we use the 20 m lattice inside the disc (81 points for b = 200 m) with bilinear interpolation at the 50 m pixel centres. A 25 m grid-shift test is reported to show the registration sensitivity.
MAD is taken about the median residual (standard definition); the paper only says 'median absolute deviation'.
The 30 m DEM is an exact area average of the native 20 m window; the pipeline cache (30.03 m pixels, rasterio average resampling) is reported separately.

PGDA-70 is a 16 px/deg simple-cylindrical grid of medians in 0.25-degree overlapping windows, gridded with GMT 'surface'; near the pole one pixel row spans all longitudes, so only a few latitude rows fall in the 40 km window and the map is heavily smoothed/interpolated there. Area medians are compared, not pixels.

Two-point slopes use the nearest pixel multiples: 60/220/560 m at 20 m, 60/240/570 m at 30 m. Grid columns run along stereographic y, which is only locally north-south; LOLA tracks near the pole run in many azimuths.
One 40 x 40 km window around the pole (high fill factor, ~20 m effective resolution); results may differ toward 80 S.

The profile reference itself is uncertain at the pole: the unweighted PGDA-70 median over the window is about 1.2x the area-weighted one (see pgda70 entries), and DEM two-point slopes differ between y columns and x rows in this window (terrain anisotropy), so the grid/profile ratio is reported both for y columns and x+y pooled.

Plane-fit slope (2-D gradient magnitude over a disc) and along-track two-point slope (one direction) are different statistics; their ratio (plane_fit_vs_profile) must not be read as an estimator error.
